title: BanG Dream! Releases Ave Mujica prima aurora Movie Commercial Featuring "Baddy Baddy"
content:
BanG Dream! released a 30-second commercial for the Ave Mujica prima aurora anime movie that features one of the band’s newest songs, “Baddy Baddy.” The song is also part of their latest mini-album , released on October 21. The movie is currently screening in Japanese theaters.

Also check out: BanG Dream! Releases “God’s Blood” from Ave Mujica prima aurora Ave Mujica prima aurora Movie Reveals 2nd Trailer

Nichicaline ( BanG Dream! Yume∞Mita ) is animating the movie with Kodai Kakimoto as director. The voice cast of the Ave Mujic a anime includes:

• Kanon Takao as Sakiko Togawa/Oblivionis

• Yuzuki Watase as Mutsumi Wakaba/Mortis

• Rico Sasaki as Uika Misumi/Doloris

• Akane Yonezawa as Nyamu Yutenji/Amoris

• Mei Okada as Umiri Yahata/Timoris

The movie is a continuation of the Ave Mujica: The Die is Cast anime, which debuted in January 2025 and was animated by Sanzigen. A sequel to the series will begin in January 2027.

The overall synopsis of the Ave Mujica anime is as follows: “Will you give me the rest of your life?” After losing everything in a single night, Sakiko Togawa reaches out toward an even deeper abyss, one that will drag everyone around her down as well. Gathering the lives of girls burdened with their own troubles and desires, Sakiko raises the curtain on a perfect masquerade. “Welcome to the world of Ave Mujica.” On a stage where sorrow, death, fear, love—even the solace of forgetting—are stripped away, will their masks be torn off and shatter into oblivion, or will they…

title: Live-Action My Sister's Boyfriend Film's Trailer Unveils Song by timelesz
content:
The official website for My Sister's Boyfriend, the live-action film of Amu Meguro 's Midori Loves My Sister ( Onē-chan no Midori-kun or literally My sister's Midori-kun ) manga, presented a new 60-second trailer and character posters for the film on Thursday. The trailer announces and previews the film's theme song "Hontō no Koto o Iu to" (If I Tell the Truth) by the group timelesz .

The original manga centers on Sui, a girl in her third year of junior high. She doesn't really get along with her older sister's boyfriend, Midori-kun, since he always treats her like a kid and makes fun of her. But Midori-kun is suddenly asked to be Sui's home tutor, and she suddenly sees an unexpected side of him.

The film has the English title My Sister's Boyfriend , and stars timelesz idol group member Masaki Hashimoto (live-action Summer Complicity ) as Midori Yukishiro, and actress Runa Nakajima (live-action Uchi no Otōto-domo ga Sumimasen ) as Sui Sanae. Rinka Kumada (live-action Otonanajimi , Kimi ni Todoke , It Takes More than a Pretty Face to Fall in Love ) plays Sui's older sister and Midori's girlfriend Momo Sanae, and Reo Matsumoto (live-action I Cannot Reach You , Propaganda Game ) plays Sui's childhood friend Ayame Mizukawa. Taisuke Niihara (live-action At 25:00 in Akasaka , Young & Fine ) plays Amamiya, a new assistant producer at the same TV station where Sui's older sister Momo works.

Mahito Kimura (live-action Strobe Edge , Blue Spring Ride series) is directing the film, and Nami Kikkawa (live-action Honey Lemon Soda film) wrote the script. Shochiku is credited for planning and overseeing the production, and is also distributing the film.

The film will open in Japan on December 4.

Meguro launched the manga in Shueisha 's Bessatsu Margaret magazine in 2022. Shueisha published the manga's 11th compiled book volume on April 23.

Meguro ended the Hinata no Blue manga in July 2021. Meguro launched the manga in Bessatsu Margaret in April 2019.

Meguro's Honey So Sweet manga ran in Bessatsu Margaret from August 2012 to November 2015. Viz Media 's Shojo Beat imprint has released the eight-volume manga in English. The series was ranked as one of Japanese Bookstore Employees' top recommended comics for 2014. The manga inspired a live-action film adaptation that opened in Japan in March 2018.

title: Cygames to Reimburse Travel, Lodging for Canceled Uma Musume Concerts
content:
Cygames announced on Wednesday that it is preparing to reimburse the travel and lodging expenses of those who were planning to attend the now-canceled Uma Musume: Pretty Derby – 7th Event World Tour: The Stage concerts in Los Angeles.

Cygames will cover cancellation fees for travel and lodging reservations, as well as travel and lodging expenses "during the target period that meet the requirements for reimbursement" for those who have already traveled to Los Angeles.

Cygames will require details such as proof of payment and receipts from those seeking reimbursement, and will announce more details about the process at a later date.

The concerts were scheduled to take place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on Thursday and Friday, but Cygames canceled the concerts on Monday after being unable to obtain U.S. visas necessary for the performance to continue.

title: 27 Years Ago, This Legendary Shonen Anime First Aired, and It’s Still Dominating the Industry
content:
Shonen anime tend to run for a long time, as has been the pattern for decades. However, no anime is bigger than the one that first aired 27 years ago and shows no signs of stopping. The anime in question is none other than Toei Animation’s One Piece , which began adapting Eiichiro Oda’s magnum opus just two years after the manga was first released. Although Oda initially planned to end the series within five years, the manga continued to grow, and so did the anime. Since its debut on October 20, 1999, the anime has followed a weekly release schedule, with breaks here and there, and evolved in many different ways.

Looking back, everything was aligned for One Piece to emerge as one of the leading anime. Toei Animation essentially aimed to replace the Dragon Ball franchise with One Piece , and it did so wonderfully, as Shueisha also recognized the potential of Oda’s creation. Throughout its run, the anime has taken a few breaks, with one of the most significant coming during the timeskip following the Marineford arc. However, the One Piece anime has evolved in recent years, and while some fans might have been disappointed by this change, it fortunately reinforces the idea that One Piece will continue airing for years to come, if not another decade.

27 Years Later, This Shonen Anime Is Still Going Strong

One Piece saw a major change in 2025 when it announced that the anime would embrace a seasonal format the following year, with a total of 26 episodes per year. In 2026, this new format was put into practice, with the anime airing from spring through the end of summer and adapting the first major events of the Elbaph arc. The intriguing aspect of this new format was that it did not significantly improve the pacing, with the anime still adapting only two to three chapters per episode. This means that even with the new format, the anime will take even longer to reach its conclusion than it would have under the old schedule. On top of that, the One Piece anime is expanding in other ways as well.

It was expected that a new anime movie was in the works, and the franchise announced just that. However, the surprise was that there would be two new anime projects, one of which would be a new canon story adapted from the manga. This is the first time the anime franchise has taken such a step, and with anime movies taking longer to produce, it further reinforces the idea that the series will continue for years to come. All these elements point to one thing: despite running for 27 years, the One Piece anime isn’t going anywhere anytime soon . While Toei Animation’s projects alone are enough to confirm the series’ longevity, the franchise is expanding in other ways, too.

Netflix announced the anime’s reboot in late 2023, and after years of silence, it is set to arrive in February 2027. The intriguing aspect is that the reboot’s first season will adapt around 60 chapters across its first seven episodes. If its development cycle follows this approach, even the reboot could continue for at least another decade. Lastly, the One Piece live-action series is thriving, with no end in sight either. The One Piece fleet, ever since the anime began in 1999, has continued to reach new horizons, and given how the franchise has developed in recent years, it is evident that this shonen series is only going to get bigger, continuing its run for the next decade and achieving what no other shonen anime could even hope to surpass.

title: Crunchyroll’s Darkest Anime of 2026 Also Has the Most Tragic Hero of the Year
content:
2026 has been an exceptional year for dark anime airing on Crunchyroll , with several series premiering since the start of the year. However, Fall 2026 has brought another dark anime that stands out even among the darkest, with a protagonist whose journey is built on a tragic childhood. While such narratives tend to soften their main characters’ suffering as new episodes are released, the second episode of this new dark series pushes its protagonist into an even more tragic situation. A protagonist like this usually emerges in seinen anime such as Vinland Saga and Attack on Titan , with even Jujutsu Kaisen earning similar recognition despite being a shonen series. Now, The Vermilion Mask is doing the same.

The new Fall seinen anime follows its protagonist as he journeys to destroy the masks his master created. This motivation stems from a tragic incident in Peru’s childhood, when he wielded a mask created by his master that drove him to kill his master and the other apprentices. Since then, Peru has been on a journey to destroy the masks, but the path has been far from easy. Now, as the second episode reveals more about the power that cost him everything, Peru is forced to lose his right hand. This loss is particularly devastating because, beyond being a human who needs his hand, Peru is a mask maker, making it an emotional blow as well.

Crunchyroll’s The Vermilion Mask Makes Its Protagonist’s Journey Even More Tragic

The Vermilion Mask episode 2 continued the harrowing events of the first episode , with the Mask of the Warrior God appearing and Sona donning it. The mask’s power was unveiled as it defeated the villain, but its next target was naturally Peru. Knowing that the Mask of the Warrior God has a time limit and a short range, Peru does his best to stay away from Sona for the time being. Despite all his efforts, Peru loses his right arm. Given that he is the protagonist, it was expected that he would get it back, but the series doesn’t follow this pattern.

Instead, the loss is permanent, but Peru doesn’t give up on his journey to hunt down and destroy his master’s masks. To hide his pain, Peru uses a happy mask, revealing that he has always relied on such elements to conceal the struggles he has endured since his childhood trauma. The loss of his arm is also significant because he used his hands to craft masks, an art that connects him to his origins as a mask creator and his master. Losing his arm should have made him abandon his mission to hunt down the masks, but Peru continues regardless.

However, the episode ends on a good note for Peru, as Sona joins him on his journey, giving him the companion he certainly needs. The Vermilion Mask will follow a protagonist who gains a companion on his otherwise solitary journey, and it might also see Peru getting his arm back. For now, however, The Vermilion Mask is the darkest anime currently airing on Crunchyroll , and it could become even darker, judging by the first two episodes and the increasingly tragic journey of its protagonist.

title: FuRyu Previews Crymelight Game's Battles in New Trailer
content:
FuRyu revealed a gameplay trailer for its CRYMELIGHT game on Wednesday. A playable demo also launched for Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5 and for PC via Steam . The video previews battles:

CRYMELIGHT is the latest installment in its CRY series of "dark bishōjo action" game series that includes the CRYSTAR game and the CRYMACHINA action role-playing game .

The game is a roguelike that will launch on November 5 for PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam . A deluxe edition of the game includes six DLC items, a digital artbook, and a digital album with 11 soundtrack songs and three voice drama tracks.

FuRyu describes the game:

Following the events of 2019's CRYSTAR and 2023's CRYMACHINA, CRYMELIGHT follows a young girl known only as “Alice” after she wakes up with no memories of her past and discovers she must journey to the lowest layer of Purgatory to earn her “Rebirth.” Alice must set out from the Tea Party Hall, defeat enemies born from the depths of madness, and confess and confront the sins she has committed, undergoing immense emotional growth in the process.

In the game, players travel between the "Wonderland" realm and "The Tea Party" realm. "Wonderland" is a prison where souls of the dead are held captive, and "The Tea Party" is a sanctuary that offers "respite to young girls burdened by their sins."

Naoki Hisaya is the plot and story supervisor, and is returning from previous entries in the CRY series. Other returning staff members from previous entries include composer Sakuzyo and animator RIRI Yamashita . YOGISYA is the character designer.

Hitomi Sekine as her character Mary performs the game's theme song "Love and Guilt."
author: ANN

title: Gundam’s Smartest Move Was Going Full Dragon Ball With This Turning Point Anime
content:
Mecha, political, space operas step aside – many fans were introduced to the Gundam franchise by the martial arts-focused, cheesy Mobile Fighter G Gundam . An anime series that felt like Dragon Ball Z in the form of giant robots. The battles and surrounding drama of the show focused more on Domon Kashu’s journey through an international tournament between Earth’s space colonies, to see who will rule the world for the next four years.

This happens to be the only real political plot point of the show, but it’s much less than muddy than some other anime’s political-heavy plots. He’s trying to carve his way through the tourney representing Neo Japan, while simultaneously attempting to find answers on the mysterious and sinister Dark Gundam and get revenge on his brother Kyoji. And it served as a major turning point for the wider Mobile Suit Gundam franchise on a whole.

G Gundam Really Changed the Game

G Gundam goes against the grain of the previous Gundam series and is in a different universe as well. Although it has its detractors, it was a brilliant move by Cartoon Network to put it on Toonami in 2002. Dragon Ball Z was heading towards the end of its massively successful run on the network, and this show couldn’t have dropped at a better time. To many, it didn’t take much to connect the dots of “Going Super Saiyan is cool, so therefore Shining Gundam leveling up each fight is cool” as well.

As simple as that sounds, it struck a chord with an audience looking for the next show beyond Dragon Ball . The comparisons were only further pushed to the forefront when the two franchises were merged in recent crossover by the Dragon Ball Super artist Toyotaro . Furthermore, it was easier to understand for the younger audiences. As much as fans love Gundam Wing now, the plot was incredibly confusing to follow (and still is to this day for some).

Also, one-on-one, martial-arts fights just hit different than long-range gun battles. An extra layer of emotion is added in when it comes to the piloting mechanics. The pilot moves the robot with his actual movements and feels the pain when his Gundam is injured. The other shows use a more traditional cockpit setup.

Gundam Fight All Set? Ready? Go!

The extra levels of cheese do make this show such an enjoyable watch. From the outset of the eye-patch-wearing on-screen narrator throwing off his blazer and yelling the above titled catchphrase, the viewer is dropped right into something they know will be over-the-top. The voice actors, specifically Domon’s, don’t care how insane the lines are. They deliver them with as much vigor as possible and further connects the viewer with the characters.

One of the things that makes Dragon Ball so great is that Goku and Vegeta’s actors sound like they are the actual characters. Without a face to look at, voice actors have to sell the character with what they have, and G Gundam followed suit, no pun intended. It also brought about its own iconic attack with Shining Finger. The soundtrack swelling, the transformation of Shining Gundam and line delivery are pure chef’s kiss.

The show doesn’t feature as many fan-favorite Mobile Suit Gundams as opposed to the other series, but it’s got some notable ones. Shining Gundam, obviously, and Master Gundam headline the show. Shining gives off much of the same protagonist Gundam vibes as Wing. A lot of red, white and blue that pops off the screen, while Master Gundam is the total opposite with its imposing horned head, darker paint job and cape that doubles as wings. It’s got that Epyon feel that just epitomizes cool but also lets the audience know that its the evil rival to Shining. The show did a great job of giving easy clues to younger viewers on who represented what.

Dragon Gundam and Spiegel Gundam are major favorites representing Neo China and Neo Germany respectively. Dragon Gundam has dragon heads that cover his hands and shoot fire from them, while Spiegel has blades that can retract under the arms and spring into action at a moments notice. There are some other honorable mentions, but unfortunately, the bulk of them are undone by stereotypes and just downright goofy builds. Neo America’s looks like a boxing football player and Neo Holland’s Gundam has a giant windmill on the front, not the best work.

G Gundam is definitely an acquired taste and one that’s doused in nostalgia, but it also has that classic anime feel that made many Americans fall in love with genre. Unfortunately, Gundam has yet to receive any additional content in this timeline . The story so far has been a one-off, but it made a gigantic impact on the franchise and its fans. Do you think G Gundam deserves more love and a chance a reboot? Let us know in the comments.

Furthermore, it was easier to understand for the younger audiences. As much as fans love Gundam Wing now, the plot was incredibly confusing to follow (and still is to this day for some).

Also, one-on-one, martial-arts fights just hit different than long-range gun battles. An extra layer of emotion is added in when it comes to the piloting mechanics. The pilot moves the robot with his actual movements and feels the pain when his Gundam is injured. The other shows use a more traditional cockpit setup.
Gundam Fight All Set? Ready? Go!

contentBlocks.text: The extra levels of cheese do make this show such an enjoyable watch. From the outset of the eye-patch-wearing on-screen narrator throwing off his blazer and yelling the above titled catchphrase, the viewer is dropped right into something they know will be over-the-top. The voice actors, specifically Domon’s, don’t care how insane the lines are. They deliver them with as much vigor as possible and further connects the viewer with the characters.

One of the things that makes Dragon Ball so great is that Goku and Vegeta’s actors sound like they are the actual characters. Without a face to look at, voice actors have to sell the character with what they have, and G Gundam followed suit, no pun intended. It also brought about its own iconic attack with Shining Finger. The soundtrack swelling, the transformation of Shining Gundam and line delivery are pure chef’s kiss.

The show doesn’t feature as many fan-favorite Mobile Suit Gundams as opposed to the other series, but it’s got some notable ones. Shining Gundam, obviously, and Master Gundam headline the show. Shining gives off much of the same protagonist Gundam vibes as Wing. A lot of red, white and blue that pops off the screen, while Master Gundam is the total opposite with its imposing horned head, darker paint job and cape that doubles as wings. It’s got that Epyon feel that just epitomizes cool but also lets the audience know that its the evil rival to Shining. The show did a great job of giving easy clues to younger viewers on who represented what.

Dragon Gundam and Spiegel Gundam are major favorites representing Neo China and Neo Germany respectively. Dragon Gundam has dragon heads that cover his hands and shoot fire from them, while Spiegel has blades that can retract under the arms and spring into action at a moments notice. There are some other honorable mentions, but unfortunately, the bulk of them are undone by stereotypes and just downright goofy builds. Neo America’s looks like a boxing football player and Neo Holland’s Gundam has a giant windmill on the front, not the best work.

G Gundam is definitely an acquired taste and one that’s doused in nostalgia, but it also has that classic anime feel that made many Americans fall in love with genre. Unfortunately, Gundam has yet to receive any additional content in this timeline . The story so far has been a one-off, but it made a gigantic impact on the franchise and its fans. Do you think G Gundam deserves more love and a chance a reboot? Let us know in the comments.

title: Nao Emoto Launches Manga of Mokuyōbi ni wa Cocoa o Novel
content:
Manga creator Nao Emoto launched a new manga based on Michiko Aoyama's Mokuyōbi ni wa Cocoa o novel on the websites for Takarajimasha 's Takarajima Sugoi! Web and Takarajimasha 's Liniere fashion and lifestyle magazine on Tuesday.

The original novel's story centers on a cafe. A barista observes that every Thursday, without fail, a woman enters the cafe and picks the same seat to order a cup of cocoa and write a letter. One day, she seems to come in with a different mood than usual.

Aoyama released the original novel in August 2017. Aoyama later released a related novel titled Itsumo no Mokuyōbi in August 2022.

Emoto launched a manga adaptation of Shinkoshoto 's Maryoku Zero no Saikyō Kenja ~Mahō Riron o Kiwametara, Sekai Saikyō ni Natteita~ ( The Strongest Sage With Zero Magic Power ~Once I Advanced Magical Theory, I Became the Strongest~) story on May 1.

Emoto previously drew the O Maidens in Your Savage Season ( Araburu Kisetsu no Otome-domo yo ) manga alongside author, anime writer, and later anime director Mari Okada . The manga launched in Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine in December 2016, and ended in September 2019. Kodansha USA Publishing released the manga in English. The manga inspired a television anime adaptation that premiered in July 2019.

Emoto drew the manga adaptation of the Josee, The Tiger and the Fish anime film (which opened in Japan in December 2020), for which she is also the character designer. Yen Press licensed the manga.

Emoto serialized her Forget Me Not romance manga, inspired by Mag Hsu 's original Taiwanese novel Mǎzimen , from 2013 to 2016. Kodansha USA Publishing also publishes Forget Me Not in English.

Emoto launched the manga adaptation of author NisiOisin 's Shin Honkaku Mahō Shōjo Risuka (The New Orthodox Magical Girl Risuka) novels in Kodansha 's Bessatsu Shōnen Magazine in April 2021, and ended it in December 2024. Kodansha published the manga's seventh and final compiled book volume in April 2024.

title: New Dragon Ball Super Remake Knocks Daima Out of the Anime’s Timeline Again
content:
Dragon Ball Super: Beerus is now in the midst of its new remake anime run this Fall, and unfortunately the newest episode has once again knocked the events of Dragon Ball Daima out of the anime’s timeline to make it all that much more confusing. As Akira Toriyama’s final project, Dragon Ball Daima set Goku on a new adventure through the Demon Realm and officially introduced previously non-canonical events like Super Saiyan 4 Goku and Super Saiyan Vegeta 3 to Toriyama’s canon. But this raised a lot of questions about Dragon Ball Super’ s own future.

Dragon Ball Super returned to screens with a brand new remake series taking on the original TV anime series from the very beginning, and with it unfortunately has once again made the anime’s timeline all the more confusing as it continues to ignore the events of Dragon Ball Daima . Because while that series had retconned new forms and ideas into the timeline from Toriyama himself, Dragon Ball Super: Beerus doesn’t really change its events with as big of changes as fans might have wanted to see from the anime .

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus Ignores Dragon Ball Daima

When Dragon Ball Super: Beerus was first announced to be an enhanced edition of the original TV anime series with new cuts, visual effects and retooled footage, there was a hope that there would be changes to address new additions from Dragon Ball Daima or previously ignored changes from the Dragon Ball Super manga release. But that’s not the case at all. For example, Dragon Ball Daima had revealed that since the fight with Majin Buu, the Supreme Kai and Kibito had found a way to defuse from the Potara Earrings that led the Kai to going on a new adventure with Goku.

Dragon Ball Super: Beerus ‘ first couple of episodes debunk this immediately with Kibitokai’s return to the anime, but there was a hope that Goku’s fight with Beerus would somehow slip in a reference to Super Saiyan 4. With the latest episode showing off the updated version of their confrontation, Super Saiyan 3 is the strongest form that Goku has at his disposal despite the fact that the end of Daima teases that Goku would be able to tap into this transformation again. Which just further throws everything into chaos.

What Does This Mean for Dragon Ball Daima ?

Despite not lining up with Dragon Ball Super’ s anime in the slightest, Dragon Ball Daima is as official of a part of the canon as any project could get. With new story, designs, and ideas coming from the late Akira Toriyama himself, there’s no better stamp on the anime than fans could ask for. That’s even less of the case with Dragon Ball Super as the anime team has its own input into its story . With this remake not making any crucial adjustments to how the original TV anime series played out, it’s only going to further brush Dragon Ball Daima under the rug.

This does sting a little bit as now Dragon Ball is moving forward without Akira Toriyama around , and that means the future of the series will likely further ignore the last of his contributions to his franchise. Dragon Ball Daima took place after Majin Buu and before Battle of Gods, and while it raised timeline questions, it more sparked a lot of potential ideas about what it could have meant for Goku and Vegeta’s future.

But that’s no longer going to be the case as Dragon Ball Super’ s anime continues with brand new arcs in the years to come. What do you think of Dragon Ball Daima no longer being a part of the anime’s timeline again? Would you want to see it addressed further? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

title: Rin Shimokawa's 'Godmother' Manga from Young Magazine US Starts Seralization on November 18
content:
The original one-shot centered on Kinryu, a college girl who is suddenly forced to drop out of college and move overseas to Japan. She goes to take care of a 114 year old grandmother whom she did not even know existed. Disgruntled and angry, she nevertheless makes it to Yokohama, and finds her grandmother living behind a mahjong parlor. There, Kinryu is forced to know about a supernatural secret that runs in the female side of her family.

Nishio launched the original one-shot as part of Kodansha 's special Young Magazine US English issue in August 2025.

The top five winners are guaranteed serialization on Kodansha 's K MANGA app. The winners will also be serialized in Japan in Monthly Young Magazine and/or YanMaga Web , serializing at the same time on K MANGA .

Other winning titles include Still You , To Dusk and Twilight , Boys Run the Riot -In Transition- , Protocol Ryugu , and The Last Terran . To Dusk and Twilight , Protocol Ryugu , and The Last Terran are all currently in serialization . The Last Terran was the most recent to start, launching in Monthly Young Magazine on August 20.

One of the winning manga, Daisuke Itabashi 's The Journey of a Dark Elf with Fading Powers , began serialization in Japan in the January 2026 issue of Kodansha 's Monthly Young Magazine in December 2025. Ray Kindō 's The Knight of Blasphemy ( Tokushin no Chevalier ) manga launched in the August issue on July 16. Seven Seas Entertainment licensed The Journey of a Dark Elf with Fading Powers , and will begin releasing it in print in March 2027.
